items.entity: thin shell on top of the design domain (load-spreading layer)
items.description: 'Structures optimization' (Fig. 6 right): the top load is 'generated by placing a thin shell at the top of the design domain'. The text never gives the shell's thickness. It also does not say whether the shell replaces the top voxel layer(s) of the 40x40x40 grid or sits above it, or whether it is a passive solid voxel layer (rho=1, E=1) or a separate plate/shell element.
readings: 1 voxel layer (1/40 of height) inside the 40x40x40 grid, fixed at rho=1 (design region 40x40x39)
1 voxel layer of passive solid added above the 40x40x40 design grid (FE mesh 40x40x41)
2 voxel layers (1/20 of height) of passive solid inside the top of the grid
no passive layer; forces applied directly to the top-face nodes of the design grid

items.entity: compressive load on the top surface
items.description: 'the top surface is subjected to distributed forces generated by placing a thin shell' (Structures optimization / Fig. 6 right). The text does not say whether the load is uniform or how it becomes nodal forces. It also does not say whether the shell works as a rigid loading plate or as a flexible layer.
readings: uniform pressure over the whole top face as consistent nodal loads (corner 1/4, edge 1/2, interior 1 weighting)
equal vertical point forces on all 41x41 top-face nodes
rigid loading plate: all top-face nodes tied to one common vertical displacement, with the total force applied to the plate

items.entity: compressive load on the top surface
items.description: No force or pressure value is given anywhere. The TO loss (Eq. 23) divides compliance by the initial compliance c0, so the magnitude only scales the reported compliance values (Fig. 7c).
readings: total force 1 spread over the top face
unit force per top-face node (total 1681 for 41x41 nodes)
unit pressure (total force = top-face area)

items.description: 'the points at the base of the design domain are fixed' (Structures optimization, Fig. 6 right). The text does not say which degrees of freedom (DOFs) are constrained, or whether all bottom-face nodes are fixed or only those under solid material.
readings: all bottom-face nodes fully clamped (ux=uy=uz=0)
bottom-face nodes fixed in the vertical direction only (frictionless platen), plus the minimum in-plane constraints needed to stop rigid-body motion
only bottom-face nodes attached to solid elements clamped

items.entity: physical size of the design domain / element size
items.description: The TO section only says '40x40x40 voxels'. The network's SDF domain is the unit cube [0,1]^3 (Methods), which implies a unit cube, but the FE length unit and element size are never stated. The 12x12x18 mm specimens are periodic arrays of cells, not the cell size.
readings: unit cube [0,1]^3, element edge 0.025
cube of 40 unit-length elements per side (element edge 1)
physical unit-cell edge in mm (e.g., 6 mm), not given

items.description: The target VFs are given, but the text does not say whether the passive top shell counts toward V and toward the reference volume for V0. A 1-voxel shell is 2.5% of the cube, which matters at VF 0.3. The constraint is applied as a soft penalty mu(V/V0-1)^2, so it acts roughly as an equality.
readings: V and V0 measured over the whole FE mesh including the shell
V and V0 measured over design voxels only (shell excluded)
shell excluded from V, but V0 = VF x the full 40^3 volume

items.description: 'Structures optimization' says the element Young's modulus comes from a 'p-norm weighted interpolation' between Emax=1.0 and Emin=1e-3 but gives no p. Methods Eq. (12) only says p 'is set as 3 in most cases'.
readings: p = 1 (linear interpolation; making densities 0/1 is left to the projection)

items.description: 'the SDF values are filtered and projected' (Structures optimization), but no filter type or radius is given. The density filter in Eqs. (13)-(14) has a radius r_d with no value, and it is unclear whether any filter is used in the latent-code TO behind Fig. 7.
readings: no filter; regularization comes only from the neural SDF and the projections in Eqs. (15)-(16)
linear (cone) density filter, r = 1.5 elements
linear density filter, r = 2 elements
linear density filter, r = 3 elements

items.entity: first SDF-to-density projection (Eq. 15 vs. constraint list of Eqs. 17-22)
items.description: Eq. (15) gives rho_bar = (e^{-alpha s}-1)(e^{alpha s}+1) = -2 sinh(alpha s). This is unbounded, so Eq. (16) can then give rho > 1 when beta is small. The problem statement after Eq. (17) instead gives rho_bar = e^{alpha s}-1, which has the opposite sign: the interior (s<0) maps to rho<0.5. alpha = 2.0 is stated.
readings: rho_bar = (e^{-alpha s}-1)/(e^{-alpha s}+1) = tanh(-alpha s/2) (probably the intended form; bounded in [-1,1] as Eq. 16 needs)
rho_bar = -2 sinh(alpha s) (Eq. 15 taken literally)
rho_bar = e^{alpha s}-1 (problem-statement version)
rho_bar = e^{-alpha s}-1 (problem-statement version with the sign corrected)

items.entity: beta continuation schedule in projection Eq. (16)
items.description: Methods: 'start from beta=1.0 and increase its value by beta=4.0 after every 30 iterations until it reaches 128'. It is unclear whether the increase is added or multiplied; neither +4 nor x4 lands exactly on 128. The 'bumps' in Fig. 7d-e come from this schedule.
readings: beta <- beta+4 every 30 iterations, capped at 128 (about 32 steps)
beta <- 4*beta every 30 iterations: 1, 4, 16, 64, then 128 (cap)
beta <- 2*beta every 30 iterations: 1, 2, 4, ..., 128

items.description: Methods: the latent code z is updated with Adam, but its learning rate and moment parameters are not given (the 5e-4 rate belongs to network training). A voxel-density solver would need OC or MMA settings instead; the SIMP section mentions both without values.
readings: Adam, lr = 1e-3, default moments (0.9, 0.999)
Adam, lr = 5e-4
Adam, lr = 1e-2
OC on voxel densities, move limit 0.2
MMA on voxel densities, standard settings

items.description: Never stated; only implied by the convergence curves in Fig. 7d-e. mu rises from 10 to 500 by 1 per iteration (490 iterations), and how long the beta schedule runs depends on its ambiguous update rule.
readings: stop when mu reaches 500 (~490 iterations)
continue until beta = 128 and relative loss change < 1e-4
fixed 500 iterations
fixed 1000 iterations

items.entity: design-space parameterization (latent codes of the full-dataset vs. filtered-dataset networks)
items.description: Fig. 7 optimizes 128-D latent codes of two neural SDF networks, one trained on the full set of 1,960 models and one on the expert-filtered set of 132. The text contains neither the network weights nor the dataset contents: blend weights were picked at random, and the isovalue sampling is described two conflicting ways ('randomly sampled within their valid interval' in Results vs. discrete Cd = 0.1..1.0, Ct = 0.1..0.9 in Methods). The filtering was a subjective expert judgment. A plain voxel-density solver has no such pattern restriction.
readings: unrestricted voxel densities (standard SIMP); the full-dataset and filtered-dataset rows of Fig. 7 become the same problem
voxel densities with periodicity (matching opposite faces) imposed to mimic a unit cell
latent-code parameterization using the authors' released networks/data
stand-in parameterization by the 7 TPMS blend weights plus isovalue Cd/Ct, solid or sheet (Eqs. 4-5)

items.description: 'Mechanical stiffness': the start is 'a structure ... randomly selected from the filtered dataset', shown only in Fig. 7a. Its TPMS blend weights, solid/sheet type, isovalue and initial VF are not given, and it has a different latent code in each network.
readings: uniform initial density equal to the target VF
the Fig. 7a TPMS structure voxelized on the 40^3 grid (parameters unknown)
the structure's trained latent code in each network

readings: 8-node trilinear hexahedra, 2x2x2 Gauss integration
